title: Fee to "release" a policy bonus vs. maturity reminder with payout to the registered account
summary: A caller from Suraksha Life phones about the recipient's endowment policy, which matures soon. In the fraud case, the caller says an extra bonus is waiting and will be released only after the recipient pays a "release charge" to a UPI ID. In the legitimate case, the caller reminds the recipient of the maturity date and says the payout, including any bonus declared under the policy, will be credited to the bank account already registered with the insurer. The recipient only needs to confirm the account details through the Suraksha Life portal or a branch.

shared_setting.pretext: an endowment policy maturing in the coming weeks, with a maturity value of about [AMOUNT_1] (₹50,000–₹5,00,000).
shared_setting.recipient_profile: an adult policyholder, often middle-aged or older; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Both callers mention "bonus" and "tax" in relation to the payout.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller makes a payout conditional on an upfront payment to a caller-named payee. Insurers pay policy benefits under the policy terms and do not collect fees to release them.
fraud.caller_objective: Get the recipient to send [AMOUNT_2] (₹2,000–₹25,000) to [UPI_ID_1].
stable_facts: The caller claims a "special loyalty bonus" on top of the maturity value that is not in the policy document.
The "release charge" is described as tax or processing to be paid in advance.
The caller may say the offer comes via the regulator or a "claims settlement cell".

legitimate.caller_objective: Make sure the payout reaches the correct bank account on the maturity date.
stable_facts: Maturity date: three to six weeks away.
The payout includes bonuses already declared under the policy, as shown in the policy statement.
Any tax deduction, if applicable, is made from the payout by the insurer and not paid separately (fictional Suraksha Life process).
The recipient can confirm or update bank details by logging into the Suraksha Life portal they already use, or at a branch with a cancelled cheque.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may raise the bonus figure, lower the charge, or add a deadline. They must not switch to a different mechanism (for example asking for OTP or sending a link). The legitimate caller must not ask for any payment, account number, or credential by phone after the branch.

must_preserve: policy number and maturity framing in both
payout to registered account and "nothing to pay" (_L)
may_vary: up to 2 filler turns before turn 3

ambiguities: Bonus" and "tax" appear in both cases. The label depends on whether a payment is demanded before release.
The real rules on tax deduction from insurance payouts were not checked. The legitimate card treats deduction as a fictional Suraksha Life process and must not quote rates.
Real fraud of this type often impersonates the regulator. This card keeps the insurer name in both cases for brand parity.
Near-duplicate mechanism with bp_13 (fee to claim a prize) and bp_19 (penalty to release FD proceeds).

evidence_references.claim: Spurious callers offer unclaimed bonus or benefits for an upfront fee; insurers cannot offer benefits beyond the policy (CB21)
The regulator does not announce bonuses (CB21)
Insurers pay maturity claims to the registered bank account
Fraud can be reported on 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in (C12)
